result.title: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds
result.summary: A vision encoder turns an image into one vector per patch, refined layer by layer. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) writes each vector of one layer as a sum of learned directions, most with a coefficient of zero. Researchers call each direction a feature and edit the encoder by removing one feature. An SAE trained from another random seed learns different features. Earlier work matches the two SAEs' features one to one by how closely their directions agree. Matched features can point alike yet respond to different image parts, so removing them may change the encoder differently. We remove a feature and, separately, its match, then compare the changes in the encoder's output on the same held out images. When the second change nearly reproduces the first, we say the removal carries across seeds. A setting fixes a DINOv2 or SigLIP layer and its SAE feature count. At our tolerance, the removal carries for 12% to 70% of matched pairs across three settings. The share is 0% in two controls: an SAE whose directions stay random and, post hoc, matches shuffled among trained features. Post hoc, predicting which removals carry is more accurate with layer contributions than with directions. Some incorrect predictions remain. One persists on independent images. So pairs can be screened at the layer. Measuring the output detects errors this screen misses.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 DINOv2 与 SigLIP 某一层的 SAE 上逐一移除特征，比较跨随机种子匹配特征在同一批图像上引起的编码器输出变化是否可“传递”，并对比方向匹配与层贡献对可传递性的预测能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「方向相似却响应不同图像区域」的诊断与消融传递性度量，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度是否真反映视觉内容、以及哪些视觉证据实际贡献于输出，但迁移到推理期状态仍需自行验证。
